claim: IgG antibodies are a homodimer of a heterodimer composed of two copies of each heavy chain (~50 kDa) and light chain (~25 kDa).
source: IgG antibodies are a homodimer of a heterodimer composed of two copies of each heavy chain (~50 kDa) and light chain (~25 kDa).
evidence: This is established knowledge about IgG antibody structure.

claim: IgG antibodies have two functional regions: the antigen-binding fragment (Fab) region at the N-terminal end and the fragment crystallizable (Fc) region at the C-terminal end.
source: They have two functional regions: the antigen-binding fragment (Fab) region at the N-terminal end and the fragment crystallizable (Fc) region at the C-terminal end.
evidence: This is established knowledge about IgG antibody structure.

claim: The two C-termini of the Fc domain are ~23 Å apart and point away from each other.
source: In the structure of IgG, the Fc domain is composed of two copies of the constant regions of the heavy chain (CH2 and CH3) forming a homodimer, in which the two C-termini are ~23 Å apart and point away from each other (Figure 1A, Left).
evidence: This structural measurement is derived from known IgG structures and presented in Figure 1A.

claim: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies are required to exhibit low nanomolar or higher antigen-binding affinity (KD <10 nM).
source: In general, diagnostic and therapeutic antibodies are required to exhibit low nanomolar or higher antigen-binding affinity (KD <10 nM) (Sliwkowski and Mellman, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sliwkowski and Mellman, 2013.

claim: Irreversibly dimerized monovalent binders can bind targets significantly better than monomeric counterparts.
source: It was shown that irreversibly dimerized monovalent binders can bind targets significantly better than monomeric counterparts (Foreman and Vilar, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Foreman and Vilar, 2017.

claim: A catAb with (KD)catenator of ~1 μM exhibited ~70-fold enhancement of the effective antigen-binding avidity in simulations with a square lattice of binding sites.
source: For instance, a catAb with (KD)catenator of ~1 μM exhibited ~70-fold enhancement of the effective antigen-binding avidity (=reduction of (KD)eff) in comparison with the same antibody without a fused catenator (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulation shown in Figure 3.

claim: The maximum fold enhancement of effective binding avidity was 41-, 73-, and 93-fold for triangular, square, and hexagonal arrays of binding sites, respectively.
source: The simulations showed that, as the connectivity number increased, the effective antigen-binding avidity increased with the maximum 41-, 73-, and 93-fold enhancement for the triangular, square and hexagonal array, respectively (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The (KD)catenator,50 was 8.0, 9.2 and 12.2 µM for the hexagonal, square and triangular array of binding sites, respectively.
source: As expected, the higher the connectivity number was, the lower (KD)catenator,50 an array exhibited; the (KD)catenator,50 was 8.0, 9.2 and 12.2 µM for the hexagonal, square and triangular array of the binding sites, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations comparing different regular arrays.

claim: At a binding site density of 11.76, the maximum fold enhancement was 1062.
source: As expected, simulations showed that higher binding site density resulted in a higher level of binding site saturation and a much more significant increase in the effective antigen-binding avidity; the maximum fold enhancement ranged from 15 (ρ=1.47)–1062 (ρ=11.76).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations for randomly distributed binding sites at different densities.

claim: At a binding site density of 58.8, the maximum fold enhancement was approximately 29,000.
source: Much greater enhancement was observed as we further increased the density of randomly distributed binding sites:~29,000 maximum fold enhancement at the ρ of 58.8 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which roughly corresponds to two-hundredths of the density of the HER2 receptor on HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells (Peckys et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1, with a citation to Peckys et al., 2019 for the HER2 receptor density comparison.

claim: SDF-1α is a small (Mr = 8 kDa) and weakly homodimerizing protein (KD = 150 µM).
source: For experimental validation, we chose stromal cell-derived factor 1α (SDF-1α) as a catenator. SDF-1α is a small (Mr = 8 kDa) and weakly homodimerizing protein (KD = 150 µM; Veldkamp et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Veldkamp et al., 2005.

claim: The sterile alpha motif (SAM) domain of SLy1 is a small (Mr = 7.4 kDa) and weakly homodimerizing protein (KD=117 μM).
source: The sterile alpha motif (SAM) domain of SLy1 is also a small (Mr = 7.4 kDa) and weakly homodimerizing protein (KD=117 μM; Kukuk et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kukuk et al., 2019.

claim: The Fab fragment of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) binds to the ectodomain of HER2 with a KD of 353 nM.
source: The Fab fragment of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) binds to the ectodomain of HER2 with a KD of 353 nM (Slaga et al., 2018), and glCV30 binds to the RBD with a similar binding affinity (not avidity, KD = 407 nM; Hurlburt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Slaga et al., 2018.

claim: glCV30 binds to the RBD with a KD of 407 nM.
source: The Fab fragment of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) binds to the ectodomain of HER2 with a KD of 353 nM (Slaga et al., 2018), and glCV30 binds to the RBD with a similar binding affinity (not avidity, KD = 407 nM; Hurlburt et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hurlburt et al., 2020.

claim: Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) exhibited a KD of 1.1 nM for HER2 in BLI experiments.
source: As a result, SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α exhibited the KD less than 0.01 nM (the limit of the instrumental sensitivity), at least 110-fold higher binding avidity compared with that of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) (KD of 1.1 nM; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α exhibited a KD less than 0.01 nM, at least 110-fold higher binding avidity compared with Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A).
source: As a result, SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α exhibited the KD less than 0.01 nM (the limit of the instrumental sensitivity), at least 110-fold higher binding avidity compared with that of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) (KD of 1.1 nM; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The association rate constants (kas) of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) and SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α were 1.9x10^5 Ms^-1 and 2.9x10^5 Ms^-1, respectively.
source: Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) and SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α exhibited similar association kinetics in bio-layer interferometry (BLI) experiments: the association rate constants (kas) of the two antibodies were 1.9x105 Ms–1 and 2.9x105 Ms–1, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments.

claim: The dissociation rate constants (kds) of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) and SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α were 2.2x10^-4 Ms^-1 and <1.0 × 10^-7 Ms^-1, respectively.
source: In contrast, the dissociation rate constants (kds) of the two antibodies were significantly different: 2.2x10–4 Ms–1 versus <1.0 × 10–7 Ms–1.
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments.

claim: SAM-glCV30/HetFc-SDF-1α increased the binding avidity by at least 130 folds compared to glCV30.
source: The glCV30 and SAM-glCV30/HetFc-SDF-1α pair also exhibited similar association and dissociation kinetics, and the catenator fusion increased the binding avidity by at least 130 folds (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A/Y100A) exhibited a KD of 243 nM for HER2.
source: To prevent the avidity enhancement beyond the instrumental sensitivity limit, we constructed triply mutated Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A/Y100A)/HetFc, which exhibited reduced binding avidity (KD of 243 nM for HER2) (Figure 6A; Bottom Left).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: SAM-Trz(3 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α (L-mScarlet) exhibited a KD of 0.8 nM, 304-fold higher binding avidity compared with Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A/Y100A).
source: As a result, SAM-Trz(3 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α (L-mScarlet) exhibited the KD of 0.8 nM, 304-fold higher binding avidity compared with that of Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A/Y100A) (Figure 6A, Bottom Middle).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 6A.

claim: SAM-Trz(3 m)/HetFc (L-mScarlet), which has one catenator arm, exhibited a KD of 373 nM, which is close to that of the mother antibody.
source: In support of the view that the observed avidity enhancement arises from the catenation of antibody molecules, SAM-Trz(3 m)/HetFc (L-mScarlet), which has one catenator arm and thus cannot catenate the antibody molecules (Figure 5A), exhibited high dissociation kinetics and the KD of 373 nM, which are close to those of the mother antibody (Figure 6A, Bottom Right).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 6A, serving as a control experiment.

claim: Obinutuzumab(Y101L) exhibited a KD of 30.4 nM for CD20.
source: In our measurement, Obinutuzumab(Y101L) exhibited the KD of 30.4 nM for CD20 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α increased the binding avidity by 234 folds compared to Obinutuzumab(Y101L).
source: As a result, SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α increased the binding avidity by 234 folds in comparison with the mother antibody.
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments.

claim: The association rate constants (kas) of Obinutuzumab(Y101L) and SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α were 3.3x10^5 Ms^-1 and 1.8 x10^5 Ms^-1, respectively.
source: This antibody/antibody-catenator pair also exhibited similar association kinetics, but significantly different dissociation kinetics: kas were 3.3x105 Ms–1 vs 1.8 x105 Ms–1, and kds were 1.0x10–2 Ms–1 vs 2.3 x10–5 Ms–1 (Figure 6B, Top).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The dissociation rate constants (kds) of Obinutuzumab(Y101L) and SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α were 1.0x10^-2 Ms^-1 and 2.3 x10^-5 Ms^-1, respectively.
source: This antibody/antibody-catenator pair also exhibited similar association kinetics, but significantly different dissociation kinetics: kas were 3.3x105 Ms–1 vs 1.8 x105 Ms–1, and kds were 1.0x10–2 Ms–1 vs 2.3 x10–5 Ms–1 (Figure 6B, Top).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α bound to the SU-DHL5 cell much more effectively than Obinutuzumab(Y101L).
source: Flow cytometric analysis showed that SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α bound to the SU-DHL5 cell much more effectively than Obinutuzumab(Y101L) (Figure 6B, Bottom).
evidence: This is a result from flow cytometry experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: glCV30-SDF-1α exhibited virtually no dissociation and enhanced the binding avidity by at least 5120 folds.
source: glCV30-SDF-1α exhibited virtually no dissociation and enhanced the binding avidity by at least 5120 folds (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: glCV30-SDF-1α exhibited an IC50 of 0.21 μg/ml in a virus neutralization assay.
source: This neutralization potency of glCV30-SDF-1α (IC50 of 0.21 μg/ml) is comparable to that (IC50 of 0.25 μg/ml) of CV30, which is an affinity-matured version of glCV30 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from the virus neutralization assay shown in Figure 7C.

claim: CV30 exhibited an IC50 of 0.25 μg/ml in a virus neutralization assay.
source: This neutralization potency of glCV30-SDF-1α (IC50 of 0.21 μg/ml) is comparable to that (IC50 of 0.25 μg/ml) of CV30, which is an affinity-matured version of glCV30 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from the virus neutralization assay shown in Figure 7C.

claim: glCV30 exhibited an IC50 of 3.22 μg/ml in a virus neutralization assay.
source: The geometric mean titer (GMT) values with a 95% confidence interval are shown on the right, which corresponds to the IC50 values of 0.25, 3.22 and 0.21 μg/ml of CV30, glCV30 and glCV30-SDF-1α, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the virus neutralization assay shown in Figure 7C.

claim: CV30 bound to the RBD domain with a KD of less than 10 pM.
source: CV30 bound to the RBD domain with the KD of less than 10 pM in our measurement by BLI, similarly as glCV30-SDF-1α did (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Fused catenators do not affect the association of antibodies but slow down the dissociation of antibodies into the bulk solution via catenation.
source: These observed kinetics are consistent with the expectation that fused catenators would not affect the association of the antibodies, but would slow down the dissociation of the antibodies into the bulk solution via catenation of the antibody molecules on the sensor tip.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the BLI experimental results showing similar association kinetics but different dissociation kinetics.

claim: The effective antigen-binding avidity of catAb depends on the density of the antigen on a target surface.
source: A thermodynamic simulation showed that quite low homodimerization affinity of a catenator, e.g. dissociation constant of 100 μM, can enhance nanomolar antigen-binding avidity to a picomolar level, and that the fold enhancement sharply depends on the density of the antigen.
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations.

claim: A catenator with a dissociation constant of 100 μM can enhance nanomolar antigen-binding avidity to a picomolar level.
source: A thermodynamic simulation showed that quite low homodimerization affinity of a catenator, e.g. dissociation constant of 100 μM, can enhance nanomolar antigen-binding avidity to a picomolar level, and that the fold enhancement sharply depends on the density of the antigen.
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations.

claim: Antibody catenation on a target surface is induced by the proximity effect where the local concentration of catAb increases due to antibody-antigen binding.
source: A proximity effect for catAb is expected on a target surface where multiple copies of target antigen are present, because the local concentration of catAb on the surface will increase owing to the antibody-antigen binding interaction. Consequently, the homodimerization between the catenator molecules will increase to form catenated antibodies in an arm-in-arm fashion (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a conceptual explanation of the mechanism supported by the model shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The effective antigen-binding affinity of catAb increases in parallel with the catenation.
source: Importantly, the effective antigen-binding affinity of catAb will increase in parallel with the catenation, and the fold enhancement would depend on the degree of the catenation.
evidence: This is a conceptual prediction based on the proposed mechanism.

claim: Catenated antibodies are not allowed to dissociate from the binding site because the catenated arms hold the dissociated antibody near its binding site, forcing it to rebind immediately.
source: Finally, the third rule is about restricted dissociation which assumes that catenated antibodies are not allowed to dissociate from the binding site, because the catenated arms would hold the dissociated antibody near its binding site, forcing it to rebind immediately (Liese and Netz, 2018).
evidence: This is an assumption in the ABM model supported by a citation to Liese and Netz, 2018.

claim: The catenation effects are sensitively affected by the binding site density.
source: Thus, the catenation effects are sensitively affected by the binding site density, in contrast with the all-or-none catenation effect observed for the regular arrays of the binding sites (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ABM simulation results shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The catenation-induced enhancement of the antigen-binding avidity was remarkably and sensitively affected by the (KD)catenator values at high binding site density (ρ>4.41).
source: In particular, the catenation-induced enhancement of the antigen-binding avidity was remarkably and sensitively affected by the (KD)catenator values at high binding site density (ρ>4.41; Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ABM simulation results shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Varying [catAb]/KD from 0.01 to 1.0 resulted in 85- to 900-fold enhancement of the antigen-binding avidity.
source: Varying [catAb]/KD from 0.01 to 1.0 (by varying KD from 10–8 to 10–6) resulted in 85- to 900-fold enhancement of the antigen-binding avidity, suggesting that the catenation effect works for a broad range of KD values (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The enhancement of (KD)eff by increasing the concentration of catAb is much less dramatic than that by increasing the affinity for catenator homodimerization.
source: Varying [catAb] from 0.1 to 10 nM resulted in far less than a 100-fold increase of (KD)eff, showing that the enhancement of (KD)eff by increasing the concentration of catAb is much less dramatic than that by increasing the affinity for catenator homodimerization (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ABM simulation results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: The broad peak fraction of glCV30-SDF-1α was highly soluble and could be concentrated at least to 200 μM.
source: The broad peak did not contain the cleaved H chain. The broad peak fraction was highly soluble, as it could be concentrated at least to 200 μM.
evidence: This is an experimental observation about the protein preparation.

claim: The avidity enhancement and strong neutralization activity of glCV30-SDF-1α reflect not only the catenation effect but also reversible oligomerization in solution.
source: We believe that the avidity enhancement and the strong neutralization activity of glCV30-SDF-1α reflect not only the catenation effect but also reversible oligomerization in solution, which further increases the binding avidity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results based on the observed behavior of glCV30-SDF-1α.

claim: Some fraction of SDF-1α likely underwent a structural change at the low pH step in the protein purification, leading to reversible heterogeneous oligomerization.
source: Likely, some fraction of SDF-1α underwent a structural change at the low pH step in the protein purification, leading to reversible heterogeneous oligomerization.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed oligomerization behavior.

claim: A catenator fused to the C-terminus of Fc would not affect the effector function Fc through the Fcγ receptor-binding site and FcRn binding site.
source: Of note, a catenator fused to the C-terminus of Fc would not affect the effector function Fc through the Fcγ receptor-binding site and FcRn binding site on it.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural location of the catenator fusion relative to the Fc receptor binding sites.

claim: The ideal catenator should geometrically disallow intramolecular homodimerization, exhibit fast association kinetics, and be able to withstand the standard low pH purification step.
source: Specifically, the ideal catenator should geometrically disallow intramolecular homodimerization, exhibit fast association kinetics, and be able to withstand the standard low pH purification step.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the experimental observations and challenges encountered.

claim: Antibody catenation can be applied to bispecific antibodies employing a heterodimeric Fc.
source: On the other hand, our demonstration indicates that this approach can be applied to bispecific antibodies employing a heterodimeric Fc.
evidence: This is an inference based on the successful demonstration with heterodimeric Fc constructs.

claim: Antibody catenation can be applied to therapeutic antibodies against viruses, which have multiple copies of target antigens on their surface.
source: First, it can be applied to therapeutic antibodies against viruses, which have multiple copies of target antigens on their surface.
evidence: This is a proposed application based on the demonstrated mechanism.

claim: Antibody catenation can be used for sandwich-type point-of-care biosensors to increase the sensitivity of detection.
source: Second, it can be used for sandwich-type point-of-care biosensors in which a second antibody is catenated to increase the sensitivity of detection.
evidence: This is a proposed application based on the demonstrated mechanism.

claim: Antibody catenation can be used to sense biomarkers that exist in a very low number on a target cell (e.g. copy number <10).
source: Third, this method can be used to sense biomarkers that exist in a very low number on a target cell (e.g. copy number <10), which requires an extremely high-binding avidity of a probe antibody.
evidence: This is a proposed application based on the demonstrated mechanism.

claim: Antibody catenation might be applied to antibody-based targeted cancer therapy to reduce side effects arising from antibody binding to normal cells.
source: Fourth, it might also be applied to antibody-based targeted cancer therapy where side effects arising from antibody binding to normal cells are a general problem. Since cancer-associated antigen molecules are lower in number on normal cells than they are on cancer cells, catenated anticancer antibodies would be concentrated on the surface of cancer cells, because the effective binding avidity of a catAb depends on the number of antigen molecules on a target surface.
evidence: This is a proposed application based on the demonstrated mechanism and the density-dependent binding behavior.

claim: Antibody catenation would greatly reduce the intrinsic toxicity of antibody-drug conjugates.
source: In particular, this approach would greatly reduce the intrinsic toxicity of antibody-drug conjugates that are widely used currently.
evidence: This is a proposed benefit based on the selective binding to high-antigen-density surfaces.

claim: The CHO-S, SU-DHL5, and HEK-293T cell lines were negative for mycoplasma.
source: The CHO-S (Gibco), SU-DHL5 (DMSZ), and HEK-293T (ATCC) cell lines were negative for mycoplasma.
evidence: This is a statement about the quality control of cell lines used in the experiments.

claim: The identity of the SU-DHL5 and HEK-293T cell lines was confirmed by Short Tandem Repeat profiling.
source: Additionally, the identity of the SU-DHL5 and HEK-293T cell lines was confirmed by Short Tandem Repeat profiling.
evidence: This is a statement about the quality control of cell lines used in the experiments.

claim: A homodimeric protein genetically fused to the C-terminus of IgG can be prevented from forming a homodimer intramolecularly by controlling the length of the connecting linker or its homodimerization affinity.
source: This structural feature indicated that a homodimer-forming protein genetically fused to the C-terminus can be prevented from forming a homodimer intramolecularly by controlling the length of the connecting linker or its homodimerization affinity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural features of IgG and the geometry of the C-termini.

claim: The fusion protein can form a homodimer intermolecularly, resulting in catenation of antibody molecules.
source: Instead, the fusion protein can form a homodimer intermolecularly, and then such a homodimerization could result in a catenation of the antibody molecules (Figure 1A, Right).
evidence: This is a conceptual prediction illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The local concentration of catAb on a target surface increases owing to the antibody-antigen binding interaction.
source: A proximity effect for catAb is expected on a target surface where multiple copies of target antigen are present, because the local concentration of catAb on the surface will increase owing to the antibody-antigen binding interaction.
evidence: This is a conceptual explanation of the proximity effect.

claim: The homodimerization between catenator molecules increases to form catenated antibodies in an arm-in-arm fashion on a target surface.
source: Consequently, the homodimerization between the catenator molecules will increase to form catenated antibodies in an arm-in-arm fashion (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a conceptual prediction illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: The fold enhancement of antigen-binding avidity depends on the degree of catenation.
source: Importantly, the effective antigen-binding affinity of catAb will increase in parallel with the catenation, and the fold enhancement would depend on the degree of the catenation.
evidence: This is a conceptual prediction about the relationship between catenation and avidity enhancement.

claim: Each binding site is presumed to be a pair of two antigen molecules (2Ag) in the ABM model.
source: To circumvent complexity, we presumed that each binding site is a pair of two antigen molecules (2Ag), and catAb make a bivalent interaction with the binding site in a 1:1 stoichiometry to form an occupied binding site (catAb-2Ag; Figure 2A, Left).
evidence: This is an assumption made in the ABM model to simplify the simulation.

claim: Catenation between two adjacent catAb-2Ag complexes requires the distance between the centers of two adjacent complexes (d) to be closer than the reach length (L).
source: For catenation to occur between two adjacent catAb-2Ag complexes, the distance between the centers of two adjacent complexes (d) should be closer than the reach length (L) defined as l+c/2, the sum of the linker length (l) and the half the catenator length (c) (Figure 2A, Right).
evidence: This is a geometric constraint defined in the ABM model.

claim: The reach length (L) is defined as l+c/2, the sum of the linker length (l) and half the catenator length (c).
source: For catenation to occur between two adjacent catAb-2Ag complexes, the distance between the centers of two adjacent complexes (d) should be closer than the reach length (L) defined as l+c/2, the sum of the linker length (l) and the half the catenator length (c) (Figure 2A, Right).
evidence: This is a definition provided in the ABM model.

claim: The equilibrium population of occupied and unoccupied binding sites is determined by the antibody's intrinsic avidity for the antigen with no effect of the catenator on the antigen-binding avidity assumed.
source: The equilibrium population of the occupied and unoccupied binding sites is determined by the antibody's intrinsic avidity for the antigen with no effect of the catenator on the antigen-binding avidity assumed.
evidence: This is an assumption in the ABM model about the first rule.

claim: The relative likelihood of the occupied state compared to the unoccupied state for any binding site is defined as [catAb]/KD.
source: Then, the relative likelihood of the occupied state compared to the unoccupied state for any binding site (the likelihood of intrinsic antigen binding) is defined as [catAb-2Ag]/[2Ag] and thus can be expressed as [catAb]/KD, where [catAb] is the concentration of catAb and KD is the dissociation constant for the bivalent catAb-2Ag interaction (Figure 2B, Left).
evidence: This is a definition in the ABM model for the first rule.

claim: The catenator was assumed to sample Vsphere uniformly in approximating the forward reaction rate.
source: In approximating the forward reaction rate, the catenator was assumed to sample Vsphere uniformly.
evidence: This is an assumption made in the ABM model to simplify the calculation.

claim: The function f(d) can be viewed as the effective local concentration of the catenator in Voverlap(d).
source: The function f(d) can be viewed as the effective local concentration of the catenator in Voverlap(d).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mathematical function f(d) in the ABM model.

claim: f(d) and the relative likelihood of catenation are sensitively affected by the reach length and limited by the catAb-catAb distance.
source: As expected, f(d) and thus the relative likelihood is sensitively affected by the reach length and limited by the catAb-catAb distance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the mathematical analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Catenated arms hold the dissociated antibody near its binding site, forcing it to rebind immediately.
source: Finally, the third rule is about restricted dissociation which assumes that catenated antibodies are not allowed to dissociate from the binding site, because the catenated arms would hold the dissociated antibody near its binding site, forcing it to rebind immediately (Liese and Netz, 2018).
evidence: This is an assumption in the ABM model supported by a citation to Liese and Netz, 2018.

claim: Antibody molecules are allowed to dissociate from the binding site only if its catenator is not engaged in homodimerization with nearby catAb-2Ag complexes.
source: Under this assumption, antibody molecules are allowed to dissociate from the binding site, only if its catenator is not engaged in the homodimerization with nearby catAb-2Ag complexes (Figure 2B, Right).
evidence: This is a rule in the ABM model illustrated in Figure 2B.

claim: The concentration of free catAb was assumed to be the same as that of total catAb in all simulations.
source: In all simulations, the number of catAb was far more than that of the binding sites, and therefore, the concentration of free catAb was assumed to be the same as that of total catAb (free catAb +antigen-bound catAb).
evidence: This is an assumption made in the ABM simulations to simplify the model.

claim: The higher the connectivity number, the lower (KD)catenator,50 an array exhibited.
source: As expected, the higher the connectivity number was, the lower (KD)catenator,50 an array exhibited; the (KD)catenator,50 was 8.0, 9.2 and 12.2 µM for the hexagonal, square and triangular array of the binding sites, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations comparing different regular arrays.

claim: Regardless of the distribution patterns, the effective antigen-binding avidity could be increased by at least 41 folds under simulation conditions with 98 binding sites.
source: Thus, regardless of the distribution patterns, the effective antigen-binding avidity could be increased by at least 41 folds under the simulation conditions where the target surface contains only 98 binding sites.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ABM simulation results for different regular arrays.

claim: Higher binding site density resulted in a higher level of binding site saturation and a much more significant increase in the effective antigen-binding avidity.
source: As expected, simulations showed that higher binding site density resulted in a higher level of binding site saturation and a much more significant increase in the effective antigen-binding avidity; the maximum fold enhancement ranged from 15 (ρ=1.47)–1062 (ρ=11.76).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations for randomly distributed binding sites at different densities.

claim: The maximal saturation and the onset (KD)catenator were considerably different depending on binding site density.
source: The maximal saturation and the onset (KD)catenator, which begins to exert the catenation effect, were also considerably different.
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations for randomly distributed binding sites at different densities.

claim: The binding site density of 58.8 roughly corresponds to two-hundredths of the density of the HER2 receptor on HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells.
source: Much greater enhancement was observed as we further increased the density of randomly distributed binding sites:~29,000 maximum fold enhancement at the ρ of 58.8 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), which roughly corresponds to two-hundredths of the density of the HER2 receptor on HER2-overexpressing breast cancer cells (Peckys et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a comparison made with a citation to Peckys et al., 2019.

claim: Varying [catAb]/KD from 0.01 to 1.0 resulted in 85- to 900-fold enhancement of the antigen-binding avidity, suggesting that the catenation effect works for a broad range of KD values.
source: Varying [catAb]/KD from 0.01 to 1.0 (by varying KD from 10–8 to 10–6) resulted in 85- to 900-fold enhancement of the antigen-binding avidity, suggesting that the catenation effect works for a broad range of KD values (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2, with an inference about the broad applicability.

claim: Varying [catAb] from 0.1 to 10 nM resulted in far less than a 100-fold increase of (KD)eff.
source: Varying [catAb] from 0.1 to 10 nM resulted in far less than a 100-fold increase of (KD)eff, showing that the enhancement of (KD)eff by increasing the concentration of catAb is much less dramatic than that by increasing the affinity for catenator homodimerization (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a result from the ABM simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: A 10-residue connecting linker, (G4S)2, was used to fuse SDF-1α to the homodimeric heavy chain of antibodies.
source: Initially, by using a 10-residue connecting linker, (G4S)2, SDF-1α was fused to the homodimeric heavy chain (H chain) of two different antibodies: Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A), a variant of the clinically used anti-HER2 antibody Trastuzumab and a germline-encoded glCV30, an antibody against the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method used.

claim: Both homodimeric antibody-catenator constructs exhibited drastic enhancements of the (KD)eff for the target proteins immobilized on the biosensor surface.
source: Both antibody-catenator constructs exhibited drastic enhancements of the (KD)eff for the target proteins immobilized on the biosensor surface.
evidence: This is a result from the initial BLI experiments.

claim: The homodimeric antibody-catenator constructs likely formed reversible heterogeneous oligomers in solution.
source: However, as described below in the 'incidental observations' section, we now believe that these constructs likely formed reversible heterogeneous oligomers in solution, and the resulting data would not be a correct reflection of the effect of antibody catenation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observations.

claim: It was possible to obviate the oligomerization problem by dually fusing a pair of two different catenators, SDF-1α and SAM, to the knobs-into-holes heterodimeric Fc.
source: It was possible to obviate the oligomerization problem by dually fusing a pair of two different catenators, SDF-1α and SAM, to the knobs-into-holes heterodimeric Fc (HetFc) (Leaver-Fay et al., 2016), via a (G4S)2 linker.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental strategy with a citation to Leaver-Fay et al., 2016.

claim: Fusion of homodimeric proteins to HetFc would result in antibody catenation on a target surface, while their catenation efficiency would be reduced compared with a corresponding homodimeric antibody-catenator construct.
source: Fusion of the homodimeric proteins to HetFc would also result in the antibody catenation on a target surface in a fashion shown in Figure 5A, while their catenation efficiency would be reduced compared with a corresponding homodimeric antibody-catenator construct.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the structural design illustrated in Figure 5A.

claim: Employing a HetFc is instrumental to generate a control antibody, which has a single catenator and can at best form a dimer but cannot be catenated.
source: Employing a HetFc is instrumental to generate a control antibody, which has a single catenator. This construct can at best form a dimer, but cannot be catenated (Figure 5A; Right).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design for a control construct illustrated in Figure 5A.

claim: While the heterodimer formation was not 100%, it was possible to purify the heterodimeric antibodies homogenously that exhibited a single elution peak from a size-exclusion column.
source: While the heterodimer formation was not 100%, it was possible to purify the heterodimeric antibodies homogenously that exhibited a single elution peak from a size-exclusion column that corresponds to the size of the heterodimer (Figure 5B and C).
evidence: This is a result from the protein purification experiments shown in Figures 5B and C.

claim: Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) and SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α exhibited similar association kinetics in BLI experiments.
source: Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A) and SAM-Trz(2 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α exhibited similar association kinetics in bio-layer interferometry (BLI) experiments: the association rate constants (kas) of the two antibodies were 1.9x105 Ms–1 and 2.9x105 Ms–1, respectively.
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments.

claim: glCV30 and SAM-glCV30/HetFc-SDF-1α exhibited similar association and dissociation kinetics.
source: The glCV30 and SAM-glCV30/HetFc-SDF-1α pair also exhibited similar association and dissociation kinetics, and the catenator fusion increased the binding avidity by at least 130 folds (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: SAM-Trz(3 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α (L-mScarlet) and Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A/Y100A) exhibited similar association kinetics but significantly different dissociation kinetics.
source: BLI analyses showed that Trastuzumab(N30A/H91A/Y100A) and SAM-Trz(3 m)/HetFc-SDF-1α (L-mScarlet) exhibited similar association kinetics, but significantly different dissociation kinetics.
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments.

claim: The observed avidity enhancement arises from the catenation of antibody molecules.
source: In support of the view that the observed avidity enhancement arises from the catenation of antibody molecules, SAM-Trz(3 m)/HetFc (L-mScarlet), which has one catenator arm and thus cannot catenate the antibody molecules (Figure 5A), exhibited high dissociation kinetics and the KD of 373 nM, which are close to those of the mother antibody (Figure 6A, Bottom Right).
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by the control experiment shown in Figure 6A.

claim: SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α was monomeric in solution.
source: Also generated was SAM-Obinutuzumab(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α (in short, SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α), which was monomeric in solution (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the size-exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α molecules were likely catenated on the surface of the SU-DHL5 cell.
source: This result indicates that the SAM-Obz(Y101L)/HetFc-SDF-1α molecules were likely catenated on the surface of the SU-DHL5 cell.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the flow cytometry results showing enhanced binding to SU-DHL5 cells.

claim: Noncovalent antibody catenation on a target surface is a way to greatly enhance antigen-binding avidity.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that noncovalent antibody catenation on a target surface is a way to greatly enhance antigen-binding avidity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from all the experimental results.

claim: The homodimeric glCV30-SDF-1α construct showed three eluted fractions from a size-exclusion column: a void, a broad peak, and a narrow peak fraction.
source: The homodimeric glCV30-SDF-1α construct showed three eluted fractions from a size-exclusion column: a void, a broad peak, and a narrow peak fraction (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a result from the size-exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The narrow peak fraction of glCV30-SDF-1α was a mixture of the L chain and H chain missing the catenator as a result of partial proteolytic cleavage.
source: The narrow peak fraction was a mixture of the L chain and H chain missing the catenator as a result of partial proteolytic cleavage.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the size-exclusion chromatography fractions.

claim: The broad peak fraction of glCV30-SDF-1α did not contain the cleaved H chain.
source: In contrast, the broad peak did not contain the cleaved H chain.
evidence: This is a result from the analysis of the size-exclusion chromatography fractions.

claim: The broad peak fraction of glCV30-SDF-1α was in a dynamic equilibrium between monomeric and oligomeric species in solution as a result of the weak intermolecular interaction of SDF-1α.
source: Assuming that the broad peak fraction was in a dynamic equilibrium between monomeric and oligomeric species in solution as a result of the weak intermolecular interaction of SDF-1α, we used it to assess their ability to enhance the binding avidity for the target antigens.
evidence: This is an assumption made to interpret the experimental observations.

claim: glCV30-SDF-1α exhibited association-dissociation kinetics similar to those of the dual catenator-fused antibodies: a similar ka but very low kd.
source: glCV30-SDF-1α also exhibited association-dissociation kinetics similar to those of the dual catenator-fused antibodies: a similar ka but very low kd in comparison with those of the mother antibody (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a result from BLI experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: glCV30-SDF-1α exhibited a~15 fold lower IC50 value compared with glCV30 in a virus neutralization assay.
source: Consistently, the glCV30-SDF-1α construct exhibited notable activity in a virus neutralization assay using vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) pseudotyped with the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein. This virus is expected to harbor multiple copies of the Spike protein on its envelope. In comparison with glCV30, glCV30-SDF-1α exhibited a~15 fold lower inhibition constant 50 (IC50) value.
evidence: This is a result from the virus neutralization assay.

claim: The neutralization potency of glCV30-SDF-1α (IC50 of 0.21 μg/ml) is comparable to that of CV30 (IC50 of 0.25 μg/ml).
source: This neutralization potency of glCV30-SDF-1α (IC50 of 0.21 μg/ml) is comparable to that (IC50 of 0.25 μg/ml) of CV30, which is an affinity-matured version of glCV30 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a comparison of results from the virus neutralization assay shown in Figure 7C.

claim: CV30 is an affinity-matured version of glCV30.
source: This neutralization potency of glCV30-SDF-1α (IC50 of 0.21 μg/ml) is comparable to that (IC50 of 0.25 μg/ml) of CV30, which is an affinity-matured version of glCV30 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the relationship between CV30 and glCV30.

claim: The avidity enhancement and strong neutralization activity of glCV30-SDF-1α reflect reversible oligomerization in solution in addition to the catenation effect.
source: We believe that the avidity enhancement and the strong neutralization activity of glCV30-SDF-1α reflect not only the catenation effect but also reversible oligomerization in solution, which further increases the binding avidity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: It is unclear why the reversible oligomerization didn't enhance the association rate constant.
source: Although it is yet unclear why the reversible oligomerization, if this is the case, didn't enhance the association rate constant, these incidental observations suggest a possible approach for producing noncovalent IgG antibody multimers that could enhance the sensitivity of diagnostic antibodies.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of an unexplained observation.

claim: The incidental observations suggest a possible approach for producing noncovalent IgG antibody multimers that could enhance the sensitivity of diagnostic antibodies.
source: Although it is yet unclear why the reversible oligomerization, if this is the case, didn't enhance the association rate constant, these incidental observations suggest a possible approach for producing noncovalent IgG antibody multimers that could enhance the sensitivity of diagnostic antibodies.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the incidental observations.

claim: The ABM model has caveats including the assumption of uniform density for the fused catenators within a sphere, which oversimplifies the dynamics of the catenators.
source: The model has caveats. First, the assumption of uniform density for the fused catenators within a sphere oversimplifies the dynamics of the catenators, which would highly depend on physical contexts, such as molecular orientations and potential intramolecular interaction with the antibody (Zhou, 2001).
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation in the ABM model with a citation to Zhou, 2001.

claim: The binding sites representing antigens are fixed on a surface in the ABM model, but in real situations, antigens move their positions.
source: Second, the binding sites representing antigens are fixed on a surface in our model, but in real situations, antigens move their positions, e.g., receptor molecules on cellular membranes (Saxton and Jacobson, 1997).
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation in the ABM model with a citation to Saxton and Jacobson, 1997.

claim: Advanced molecular dynamics simulations incorporated into the ABM would take account of microscopic details to result in a more accurate prediction.
source: Advanced molecular dynamics simulations incorporated into the ABM would take account of these microscopic details to result in a more accurate prediction of the behaviors of the catAb molecules and the binding sites.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future improvements to the model.

claim: Despite the caveats, the simulations provided valuable insights into the proper ranges of the antigen-binding avidity of an antibody and catenator-catenator binding affinity.
source: Despite these caveats, the simulations provided valuable insights into the proper ranges of the antigen-binding avidity of an antibody and catenator-catenator binding affinity.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the simulations despite their limitations.

claim: According to the simulation, SDF-1α and SAM were adopted as catenators, both of which are weakly homodimerizing proteins (KD of 100–150 μM).
source: According to the simulation, we adopted SDF-1α and SAM, as catenators, both of which are weakly homodimerizing proteins (KD of 100–150 μM).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental strategy informed by the simulation results.

claim: When fused to antibodies, SDF-1α and SAM resulted in great enhancement of the effective antigen-binding avidity due to drastically reduced rate of dissociation.
source: When fused to antibodies, they resulted in great enhancement of the effective antigen-binding avidity of the antibodies, which was due to drastically reduced rate of dissociation of the fused antibody molecules from the immobilized antigens.
evidence: This is a summary of the experimental results.

claim: Cancer-associated antigen molecules are lower in number on normal cells than they are on cancer cells.
source: Since cancer-associated antigen molecules are lower in number on normal cells than they are on cancer cells, catenated anticancer antibodies would be concentrated on the surface of cancer cells, because the effective binding avidity of a catAb depends on the number of antigen molecules on a target surface.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact about cancer-associated antigens.

claim: Catenated anticancer antibodies would be concentrated on the surface of cancer cells because the effective binding avidity of a catAb depends on the number of antigen molecules on a target surface.
source: Since cancer-associated antigen molecules are lower in number on normal cells than they are on cancer cells, catenated anticancer antibodies would be concentrated on the surface of cancer cells, because the effective binding avidity of a catAb depends on the number of antigen molecules on a target surface.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the demonstrated density-dependent binding behavior.

claim: A higher (or at least the same) catenation effect should be observed for the conventional homodimeric IgGs compared to dual catenator-fused heterodimeric IgGs.
source: While we demonstrated that dual catenator-fused heterodimeric IgGs can enhance binding avidity, a higher (or at least the same) catenation effect should be observed for the conventional homodimeric IgGs.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the structural considerations.

claim: To prevent the oligomer formation of the homodimeric IgGs or potential intramolecular homodimerization of the catenator, a more robust catenator has to be employed.
source: To prevent the oligomer formation of the homodimeric IgGs or potential intramolecular homodimerization of the catenator, a more robust catenator has to be employed.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the experimental challenges encountered.
